title: gen fns and generators — the Vyrn guide

chapter.title: gen fns and generators
chapter.lede: A `gen fn` is ordinary Vyrn that runs while the program compiles and returns Vyrn source. RPC, UI, i18n, OpenAPI and GraphQL are libraries built this way. None of them is a compiler feature.

sections.heading: gen fns
prose: A generator is a function marked gen. It returns a String of Vyrn source. It may read files through readFile and listDir, scoped to the paths its caller passed in, and it may not write, use module state, or reach an extern.
This one writes a lookup table. It takes no input, so its answer is the same on every machine — which is the property a build has to have.
There is no run link on this block. A generator is not a program: it needs the file that imports it, and the playground takes one source.

sections.heading: Generator imports
prose: The target of an import can be a call to a generator. The compiler runs the call at load time, caches it, and links the source it returned as an ordinary module. Everything after that is normal Vyrn.
vyrn emit-gen <file> prints the source a generator produced.
This page is built the same way. A generator reads std/ and writes the reference pages.

sections.heading: Reflection
prose: schemaOf() reads a validated type's own declaration. It answers with the name, the base type, the documentation line and every bound the where clause implies. jsonSchema() writes the JSON Schema document from the same facts.
This is not runtime reflection. Vyrn erases types before the program runs; the compiler computes the answer from the declaration.
